content: This document does not contain all the information available about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your use. The information provided is not a substitute for personalized medical advice and should not replace the guidance of your healthcare professional. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. FDA Warning: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) advises against using quinine to treat leg cramps. It has not been proven effective for this purpose and may cause serious side effects. Uses: This medication is used alone or in combination with other drugs to treat malaria, a disease caused by mosquito bites in regions where malaria is common. Malaria parasites enter the body through mosquito bites and reside in tissues such as red blood cells or the liver. This medication targets and kills malaria parasites living in red blood cells. In some cases, additional medications like primaquine may be required to eliminate parasites in other tissues. Both drugs may be necessary for a complete cure and to prevent relapse. Quinine belongs to a class of drugs called antimalarials. The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) provides updated guidelines and travel recommendations for malaria prevention and treatment worldwide. How to Use: Before starting quinine, read the Medication Guide and any Patient Information Leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Take this medication 2 to 3 hours before or after consuming antacids containing aluminum or magnesium. The dosage and duration of treatment depend on your medical condition, the country where you were infected, other medications you may be taking for malaria, and your response to treatment. It is crucial to take this medication (and any other malaria medications) exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Do not take more or less than the prescribed dose, and do not skip doses. Continue taking the medication until the full prescribed amount is finished, even if symptoms improve after a few days. This medication works best when its levels in your body are kept constant, so take it at evenly spaced intervals. Inform your doctor if you do not start feeling better after 1 to 2 days of starting this medication. Side Effects: Common side effects may include mild headache, flushing, unusual sweating, nausea, ringing in the ears, decreased hearing, dizziness, blurred vision, and temporary changes in color vision. Quinine may also cause low blood sugar (hypoglycemia), especially during pregnancy. Symptoms of low blood sugar include sudden sweating, shaking, rapid heartbeat, hunger, blurred vision, dizziness, or tingling in the hands or feet. If these symptoms occur, raise your blood sugar by consuming a quick source of sugar such as sugar, honey, candy, fruit juice, or non-diet soda. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Precautions: Before taking quinine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, or to related drugs like quinidine or mefloquine, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. Quinine may cause dizziness or blurred vision. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can worsen these effects. Avoid driving, using machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness or clear vision until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. Quinine may cause a condition affecting heart rhythm (QT prolongation). The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other drugs that can cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood may also increase your risk of QT prolongation. This risk may be higher if you use certain drugs (such as diuretics or water pills) or if you have conditions like severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. Discuss the risks, benefits, and treatment options with your doctor. This drug passes into breast milk but is unlikely to harm most nursing infants. Your doctor may test your infant for a specific enzyme deficiency (glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency, or G6PD) before you breastfeed. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Other medications can affect the removal of quinine from your body, which may impact how quinine works. Similarly, quinine can slow the removal of other medications from your body, potentially affecting their effectiveness. Many drugs besides quinine may affect heart rhythm (QT prolongation), including amiodarone, dofetilide, mefloquine, pimozide, procainamide, quinidine, sotalol, and macrolide antibiotics (such as erythromycin), among others. Quinine is very similar to quinidine. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests (such as urine tests for catecholamines, protein, or steroids), possibly causing false test results. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Lab Tests and Monitoring: While taking this medication, your doctor may order lab and/or medical tests (such as G6PD blood levels, vision tests, blood potassium, liver/kidney function, or EKG) to monitor your progress and check for side effects. Keep all medical and lab appointments. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is more than 4 hours after the missed dose, skip it and take your next dose at the regular time. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Note: This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
